_schema.description: Normative threat/control/verification matrix for plaudon. Checked by scripts/check-threat-model.py and crates/security/tests/threat_model_traceability.rs. Edit this file, then run `python3 scripts/check-threat-model.py --update` to regenerate the Markdown table in docs/threat-model/README.md.

status_values.implemented: Control exists in this repository and every listed verification test exists and runs in CI.
status_values.open: Control is partially present. The listed verification tests exist and cover the implemented part; the named gap is restated in open-findings.md.
status_values.planned: Control is not present in this repository yet. Owner names the module that will implement it; verification MUST be empty (no invented test names).

rules: ids are TM-001.. and strictly sequential in array order
every string in spec_threats is matched by exactly one row.threat (verbatim SPEC §16.2 threat column)
verification entries are Rust test-function names only, and each must resolve to a `fn <name>(` definition in the repository
owner must be an existing path unless status == planned
every planned/open row must appear in docs/threat-model/open-findings.md

spec_threats: Legacy BLE cleartext audio and static credential
Device source depleted by phone transfer

rows.threat: Credential disclosure
rows.control: Keychain/Credential Manager; no plaintext DB; redacted logs
rows.notes: The keychain-backed store, the opaque-reference database contract and the redaction of secret-bearing Debug/Display output are in place. Remaining gap: the crash-report scan named in the §16.2 verification column, which needs the diagnostics reporter.

rows.threat: Legacy BLE cleartext audio and static credential
rows.control: Compatibility warning, explicit local-only does not imply over-the-air encryption, no raw GATT payload logs
rows.notes: The disclosure is machine-enforced: NOT_GUARANTEED carries the radio-layer statement and every policy snapshot returned to the UI includes it. Suppression of raw GATT payload logging belongs to crates/plaud-ble and is not implemented (App. B.5, B.7).

rows.threat: Spoofed PLAUD BLE advertisement
rows.control: Do not authorize from local name/manufacturer alone; authenticate device profile and user-selected identity, fail closed on mismatch
rows.notes: Device/transport workstream; no epic letter assigned in this workspace. Identity assurance may only be labelled `profile-authenticated` (App. B.5).

rows.threat: Firmware handshake downgrade
rows.control: Mode detection and strict profile selection; no fallback from newer encrypted mode to legacy cleartext
rows.notes: App. B.5 mode-B RSA/ChaCha20-Poly1305 pre-handshake: implement with lawful credentials and test vectors, or mark the firmware unsupported. Never downgrade.

rows.threat: Device-side destructive sync
rows.control: Strict read-only opcode allowlist, prohibit delete/clear/write-settings/OTA, no auto-ack before verification
rows.notes: §6.3 invariant 14 and App. B.6. Compile-time opcode allowlist distinct from any future device-settings plugin.

rows.threat: Device reconnect wrong identity / replay
rows.control: Per-device vault records, transfer binding and identity/firmware revalidation
rows.notes: Depends on the per-device vault entries of §16.4 (TM-034).

rows.threat: Cloud request in Local-only Mode
rows.control: Rust outbound policy blocks PLAUD HTTP, OpenRouter and optional model fetches
rows.notes: §6.3 invariant 15. The gate is deny-by-default and is the only way to obtain an EgressTicket, which the HTTP transport and the process launcher both require. An OS-level monitor now observes a real local import run and asserts zero app-initiated connections; an unobserved run fails the fixture instead of passing silently.

rows.threat: Device source depleted by phone transfer
rows.control: Mark source as incomplete/unsynced-only; never infer historical completeness
rows.notes: App. B.3/B.8: an empty or short delta list is not evidence of an empty device.

rows.threat: Arbitrary command execution
rows.control: No generic shell; typed fixed CLI args; version check
rows.notes: GatedCommand accepts only CliArg values built from a validated identifier vocabulary; the program is pinned to PLAUD_CLI_PROGRAM and no shell is ever interposed. The §16.2 verification column's `fuzz command args and malicious titles` is covered by the corpus replay.

rows.threat: Signed URL leak
rows.control: Ephemeral memory only; URL scrubber
rows.notes: Scrubbing holds at both ends: Debug for a gated request renders no URL, header or body, labels keep scheme+host+port only, and a command response carrying a signed URL or bearer token is rejected before it reaches the UI. Remaining gap: the repository-wide log and crash-report scanner over emitted diagnostics (crates/diagnostics).

rows.threat: SSRF via redirect
rows.control: HTTPS/allowlist; DNS/IP safety; bounded redirects
rows.notes: Destination::url enforces https-only, rejects embedded credentials, rejects IPv4/IPv6 literals and loopback/private/mDNS hostnames, and the host allowlist matches on label boundaries. Redirect following is a property of the not-yet-written HTTP transport implementation: each hop must be re-authorized through the gate and the hop count bounded.

rows.threat: Malicious audio decoder input
rows.control: Untrusted input sandboxing where feasible; patched codecs; resource caps
rows.notes: Implemented half: untrusted media decoding and model inference run out of process behind plaudon_security::sandbox::SandboxedHelper. The parent grants an explicit canonicalised read/write path set, a memory cap, a CPU-seconds cap and a wall-clock deadline; network access and further exec are not expressible as grants in V1 (NetworkAccess::Denied, ExecAccess::DeniedBeyondHelper are one-variant enums). The helper boundary is a length-prefixed JSON protocol carrying only strings, integers, booleans and enums, with no pointer, descriptor or platform handle crossing it. A killed, timed-out or OOM helper becomes Recoverable/Terminal and is persisted as FailedRetryable/FailedTerminal; Completed is only constructible from a response the helper actually sent (§14.1, §14.7). Denials are proven to come from the OS, not from a cooperative helper: the same probe binary succeeds at the same out-of-grant read under IsolationPreference::ResourceCapsOnly. Per-platform assurance, which must not be generalised: macOS (verified on macOS 26 arm64) restricts filesystem, network and exec through a generated deny-by-default Seatbelt profile run via /usr/bin/sandbox-exec, a primitive Apple has deprecated and which is probed at every launch, degrading to ReducedIsolation{PrimitiveUnavailable}; macOS has no hard kernel memory cap, because the kernel rejects RLIMIT_AS/RLIMIT_DATA below the dyld shared cache reservation, so the memory cap is enforced by the parent sampling the child's resident set every 20 ms and terminating on breach, which is real enforcement with a sampling delay; macOS CPU and wall clock use RLIMIT_CPU plus a parent-side monotonic deadline. Windows uses a real job object (process memory limit, one active process, kill-on-job-close, job time, basic UI restrictions), assigns the helper to the job immediately after creation rather than creating it suspended (no untrusted work happens in that window because the helper does nothing before its first IPC frame, which the parent sends only after assignment), and applies no filesystem or network restriction in V1, reported as ReducedIsolation{PrimitiveUnavailable}. Other unix platforms get POSIX resource limits only and report ReducedIsolation{PlatformUnsupported}; Landlock is deliberately not claimed. Residual risk: kernel vulnerabilities, the input and output files the helper is legitimately granted, and anything outside this process - the sandbox is per-helper and says nothing about other processes on the machine. The limitations are machine-readable at run time through IsolationReport.notes (the plaudon_security::sandbox::NOTE_* constants) and IsolationReport::summary(), which always appends the note count. Remaining gap: the §16.2 `patched codecs` half and the AFL/libFuzzer corpus plus sanitizer runs over a real decoder, which need the EPIC F audio pipeline, and a signed entitled helper under the macOS App Sandbox as the durable replacement for sandbox-exec.

rows.threat: Supply-chain compromise
rows.control: Lockfiles, SBOM, pinned hashes/signatures, SCA
rows.notes: Cargo.lock is committed and the workspace pins versions centrally. SBOM generation, cargo-deny/OSV scanning and artifact hash pinning are release-tooling work with no owner in this workspace.

rows.threat: Unwanted cloud transfer
rows.control: Central dispatch policy; consent token; default local
rows.notes: Central dispatch, default-local and the scoped consent token are all enforced, in that order: the egress gate decides before consent is consulted, so a grant can never widen Local-only Mode, and an approval carries the EgressTicket that the transport requires.

rows.threat: Prompt injection in transcript
rows.control: Transcript treated as data; schema checks; no external tools
rows.notes: §6.3 invariant 8 and §9.6. The egress gate contributes the `no external tools` half structurally: an inference helper cannot open a socket without a ticket (TM-026).

rows.threat: Unauthorized frontend file access
rows.control: A closed typed command surface with no generic shell, HTTP or filesystem command, plus server-side path validation
rows.notes: The threat wording is the SPEC §16.2 one and predates the egui cutover (ADR-0024); the user interface is now in process and there is no IPC boundary, so `frontend` means the view layer. Both halves of the control hold without a capability manifest: the published surface is generated from one table in crates/app/src/command.rs, so a command cannot be added to the dispatcher without appearing in COMMAND_NAMES, and no generic-execution name is representable; and every path-shaped argument goes through crates/app/src/validate.rs before a port sees it, where a view-supplied string can never become an approved handle and every accepted path resolves inside a permitted root.

rows.threat: Local plaintext data exposure
rows.control: OS disk encryption guidance; future encrypted vault; warn on plaintext backup
rows.notes: §13.7 keeps the archive plaintext-on-disk for V1 by design; the control is honest disclosure plus the §13.8 encrypted portable archive. No forensic-erasure claim is made anywhere (see README).

rows.threat: Watched-folder file loss
rows.control: Copy-only staging, readiness probe, immutable archive; no source deletion
rows.notes: §6.3 invariant 11, App. A.4. The staging primitive this control depends on is implemented in crates/security/src/fsguard/tempdir.rs: staging copies, the source file is byte-identical afterwards, commit is a same-volume rename and an abandoned staging file is removed. Remaining gap: the watcher itself — readiness probe, placeholder handling and the mid-copy/rename chaos tests (EPIC K).

rows.threat: Unofficial PLAUD login flow
rows.control: Official CLI only, no bearer-token copy/paste or browser extension bridge
rows.notes: The launcher will start exactly one pinned program (PLAUD_CLI_PROGRAM) and nothing else, which structurally excludes a scraping helper. The UI-side refusal to accept a pasted bearer token belongs to the desktop onboarding flow (EPIC E).

rows.threat: Remote deletion propagation
rows.control: Explicit tombstones; remote deletes cannot cascade into archive
rows.notes: §6.3 invariant 11, §7.10, App. A.2.

rows.threat: Local automation escape
rows.control: No unauthenticated localhost server; OS user-level permissions and typed commands
rows.notes: §6.3 invariants 12 and 13. The architecture already excludes a listener: nothing in the workspace binds a socket, and the egress gate covers outbound initiation only.

rows.threat: Restored archive injection
rows.control: Decompression bounds, path validation, checksums, schema verification
rows.notes: Decompression bounds and path validation are implemented and fuzzed: traversal, absolute and device-namespace entries, case- and NFC-folded duplicates and compression-ratio bombs are all refused, validation never touches the filesystem, and a symlink planted between inspection and extraction is caught at target resolution. Remaining gap: manifest checksums and backup schema verification, which belong to the EPIC J restore path.

rows.threat: Insecure auto-update
rows.control: Signed artifacts; verified release manifest; rollback strategy
rows.notes: §16.5. The egress side is already closed: an update check is a distinct EgressPurpose that Local-only Mode refuses (TM-026). Signature verification and rollback policy are packaging work, and they now belong to apps/plaudon-egui and its two packaging scripts (ADR-0024): no notarized macOS build and no Authenticode-signed Windows build exists yet, because we hold no credentials, and both scripts exit 3 rather than report a status they did not earn.

rows.threat: Excessive telemetry
rows.control: Opt-in; no sensitive content; aggregate only
rows.notes: Opt-in is enforced structurally: telemetry is denied unless the grant records an explicit opt-in, and it is denied outright in Local-only Mode. `No sensitive content; aggregate only` needs a payload builder that does not exist; there is no telemetry sender in the repository today.

rows.threat: Cost explosion
rows.control: User budgets + provider guardrails + uncertain-job safeguards
rows.notes: §10.4, §10.7. An uncertain outcome must be recorded as unknown rather than silently retried.

rows.threat: App-initiated network egress while Local-only Mode is on
rows.control: A single Rust-owned OutboundPolicy gate used by every network-capable subsystem (PLAUD CLI, OpenRouter, model manager, update checker, telemetry, future helpers); deny by default; every decision recorded
rows.notes: §1.5 `Direct-device transfer privacy` and §22.15. A fresh installation starts local-only, the mode overrides both the import route and the processing destination, and a cloud-synced watched folder is disabled with an explanation rather than silently trusted. The OS-level monitor now runs a real local import under observation, a negative control proves the fixture can fail, and an unobserved run is reported as monitor-unavailable rather than as a pass. The evidence bundle states its own limits (§24).

rows.threat: PLAUD Cloud CLI subprocess launched in Local-only Mode
rows.control: The cloud CLI is a separate executable with its own network stack, so it is never invoked in Local-only Mode; launch requires an EgressTicket and the environment is scrubbed
rows.notes: §22.15 requires that Local-only Mode never launches the CLI. The gate refuses the launch, and the OS-level monitor independently fails any observed run in which the CLI program is executed, matching on the program leaf so a renamed path cannot hide it.

rows.threat: Legacy BLE radio-layer disclosure presented as covered by Local-only Mode
rows.control: Every effective-policy snapshot carries the explicit statement that disabling internet access adds no radio-layer confidentiality; the same statement is reproduced in user-facing documentation
rows.notes: Machine-enforced in the policy snapshot and in these documents. The Devices screen copy that must repeat it (App. B.8) is EPIC E work and does not exist yet.

rows.threat: Device identity assurance overclaimed as cryptographic verification
rows.control: Label identity assurance `profile-authenticated` unless the protocol actually proves cryptographic identity; no `Supported` compatibility cell without a hardware evidence record
rows.notes: App. B.2/B.5. Enforced today only by review of documentation language; see README `What this threat model does not guarantee`.

rows.threat: Expired or revoked consent grant still passes the dispatch preflight
rows.control: Consent is a scoped capability (purpose, content type, model/provider set, retention/routing, disclosure version) re-checked at dispatch time; revoked or expired grants fail closed
rows.notes: §6.3 invariant 5. The preflight re-checks the grant at dispatch time against an injected clock; revocation is recorded and final, and a backwards clock cannot resurrect a revoked grant.

rows.threat: Destination, purpose or privacy posture changes without re-prompting
rows.control: Re-prompt when destination/purpose/privacy posture or disclosure version changes; an unresolved posture blocks dispatch
rows.notes: Destination, route, content type and retention posture are all scope axes, and an unknown posture never satisfies a requirement. Remaining gap: no named test covers re-prompting when only the disclosure version changes, although NetworkGrant already records one.

rows.threat: Consent inferred from the mere presence of an API key
rows.control: A stored OpenRouter key never implies permission to send content; permission comes from an explicit scoped grant
rows.notes: A stored key is not an input to the preflight at all, and an `ask every time` posture can never be satisfied without a fresh decision.

rows.threat: Plaintext credential fallback when the OS secret store is unavailable
rows.control: macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager only; an unavailable store yields an actionable locked state, never a silent downgrade
rows.notes: SECRET_STORE_LOCKED / SECRET_STORE_FAILED / SECRET_NOT_FOUND are distinct outcomes, and no code path substitutes a file or in-memory value for an unavailable platform store. See ADR-0014.

rows.threat: Universal or shared BLE token reused across devices
rows.control: Per-device vault entries keyed by device identity; universal/global tokens prohibited; DB and backups hold opaque references only
rows.notes: App. B.7 and §22.9. Vault entries are device-scoped by construction, a wildcard or shared scope is not constructible, and the backup projection of the database carries references only.

rows.threat: Secrets reach environment variables, argv, crash traces or SQLite
rows.control: Scrubbed subprocess environment, no secret-bearing CLI arguments, no secrets in persisted state or diagnostics
rows.notes: Environment, argv and SQLite are covered: a secret is not representable as a CLI argument, the child environment is scrubbed, and a credential-shaped value in any database column fails the fixture. Remaining gap: the crash-trace scan, which needs the diagnostics reporter.

rows.threat: Transient secret buffers linger in process memory
rows.control: Zeroize transient buffers where feasible, and state plainly that in-process memory cannot be perfectly protected from privileged malware
rows.notes: The honesty half is already published: the memory statement is item 5 of NOT_GUARANTEED and is reproduced in README.

rows.threat: Path traversal or non-canonical path accepted at a trust boundary
rows.control: Canonicalize at the boundary, confine to managed roots, use private temp directories, reject traversing archive entries
rows.notes: Canonicalization happens at the boundary against an explicit root set, symlinks and junctions are resolved before the containment check and their targets are not opened on rejection, Windows device names and UNC/NUL forms are refused, and staging uses owner-only private temp directories. The rejection envelope never echoes the candidate path.

rows.threat: Managed data directory readable by other local users
rows.control: Restrictive permissions on the managed data directory and on staged temp files
rows.notes: Permissions are applied at creation, not after writing: the managed data directory and every private staging directory are owner-only, and two concurrent staging directories never collide.

rows.threat: Production build ships a debuggable artifact or an escape hatch out of the platform's runtime protections
rows.control: The packaging scripts audit the artifact they produce: no hardened-runtime escape hatch, no debugger entitlement, exactly the five reviewed macOS privileges, an asInvoker Windows manifest, and a fail-closed exit without a signing credential
rows.notes: §6.3A. Restated at the egui cutover (ADR-0024). The original wording was a webview one — devtools, a content security policy, remotely hosted UI content, the shell plugin — and none of those exist in a Rust-only binary: there is no browser engine, no CSP and no capability manifest, so the plaudon-tauri-audit binary and crates/security/src/tauri_guard/audit.rs were deleted rather than re-pointed. The property they protected is that a published artifact must not be inspectable or escalatable; in a native build that is an entitlement and manifest question. scripts/package-macos-egui.sh refuses to package a bundle whose entitlements request JIT, unsigned executable memory, a library-validation opt-out, dyld environment variables, a debugger, get-task-allow, camera or audio input, and audits the granted set again after signing with codesign -d --entitlements -; scripts/package-windows-egui.ps1 asserts the embedded manifest requests asInvoker with uiAccess=false and that the installer writes nothing to HKLM. The tests above assert the same inputs on both platforms.

rows.threat: Cloud processing is not visibly distinguishable from local processing
rows.control: Per-route labelling in the UI (route and processing destination shown separately), `Cloud: not used` only when the route is genuinely cloud-independent
rows.notes: App. B.7/B.8. EffectiveNetworkPolicy already serializes the per-capability reasons the UI needs. The egui shell renders the sentence from the DTO's own cloud_route in exactly one place, so a screen cannot print `Cloud: not used` on its own authority. Remaining: the same per-route labelling on the recording and job surfaces, not only on the device transfer screen.

rows.threat: Local-only Mode or provider zero-retention presented as a compliance or residency guarantee
rows.control: Documented non-claims enforced in CI: a prohibited-assurance-language list is checked against every threat-model document, and every NOT_GUARANTEED statement is reproduced verbatim
rows.notes: §16.6 and §23 reference accuracy notes. The same two checks run from scripts/check-threat-model.py for the docs-only CI job.

rows.threat: Error envelope leaks a credential, signed URL, request body or transcript excerpt
rows.control: Every security error crosses into the application taxonomy through one mapping module onto the closed AppErrorCode set; the user-facing message is chosen by the domain code and the security layer's specific reason travels only in AppError::detail, which is never shown to the user and never carried into an event
rows.notes: §15.4 forbids signed URLs, credentials, raw request bodies and transcript excerpts in an envelope. The single bridge makes that true by construction rather than by review: there is exactly one place where a security error becomes an AppError, every security code maps onto a member of the closed 50-code domain set, and the detail string is built from fixed vocabulary plus already-redacted labels. Retryability is part of the mapping, so the job engine can persist a recoverable state for a killed helper instead of inventing one (§14.1).

rows.threat: Diagnostic redactor leaves embedded URLs and separator-bearing credentials in persisted text
rows.control: Every diagnostic record and unmapped vendor string passes through one redactor before persistence; a URL anywhere in a token and any opaque credential shape are replaced, not only space-delimited bare-scheme tokens
rows.notes: Raised by D2.4 fuzzing against plaudon_domain::error::Redactor, which AppError::from_unmapped_vendor and DiagnosticLog::record both run untrusted vendor text through before it is persisted. Two defects: redact_token only matches a scheme at the start of a token, so `see (https://…)`, a quoted URL, an angle-bracketed URL or `url=https://…` survive verbatim including a signed query string; and looks_like_opaque_secret requires every character to be [A-Za-z0-9_-], so a dotted JWT and standard base64 credentials survive. The cited regression test asserts the contract as it should hold and is #[ignore]d with a reason pointing at this finding, so it turns green and the ignore can be deleted the moment the fix lands; reproducers are committed under tests/fixtures/fuzz-corpus/domain_redactor/. Team-AB has confirmed both defects and has a fix on epic-a-spikes (URL matched anywhere in the token, segment-splitting on . & ? , ; with a [A-Za-z0-9-_+/=] alphabet); it is not in this tree yet.

rows.threat: Voice profile embedding leaves the device through any egress path (cloud dispatch, model download, telemetry, diagnostics or a notification payload)
rows.control: Speaker embeddings get their own egress payload class, VoiceBiometric, which OutboundPolicy::authorize refuses in every network mode for every subsystem with no consent scope that could permit it; the local-only egress watch is extended to the enrol-and-match flow, and diagnostics redaction treats profile names like transcript text and embedding bytes as unloggable
rows.notes: Planned by docs/specs/VOICE_PROFILES_SPEC.md (VP-110 to VP-113) and ADR-0080. The feature is local-only in and out of Local-only Mode; unlike TranscriptText and AudioBytes, the new payload class is unconsentable by construction, so a future coding mistake that requests the egress is refused structurally rather than by review. The P1.4 change added the voice_embedding shape to the section 6.3A response scanner (crates/security/src/response.rs), so a serialized result carrying an embedding-named field is already refused; the payload class, egress watch and diagnostics redaction remain to be built.

rows.threat: Embedding inversion or re-identification from a stolen voice-profile store
rows.control: Embedding vectors exist at rest only as XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext under a feature-scoped key in the OS secret store (new SecretScope::VoiceProfileKey); an unavailable store is a locked feature per ADR-0014, never a plaintext fallback; embeddings are excluded from exports by default; the documents state honestly that encryption protects data at rest, not data in use
rows.notes: Storage leg implemented (P1.2): migration 0900 keeps embeddings only as XChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext bound to person+model+dimension as AEAD additional data, the key lives in the OS vault under SecretScope::VoiceProfileKey, an unavailable vault locks the biometric tier while the name-only roster keeps working (ADR-0014, spec §12.2A), and destroying the key is the VP-095 cryptographic erasure. The matching job keeps the same rule in flight: its per-cluster scratch (migration 0901) is ciphertext bound to job, run and cluster and is destroyed when the job settles. Gap: the export/backup exclusion of embeddings is not built yet (tracked by TM-046), and encryption protects data at rest, not data in use — vectors are plaintext in process memory while a job runs.

rows.threat: Profile export leaks voiceprints outside the user's control (plaintext backup, metadata export or an archive restored on another machine)
rows.control: Voice data is excluded from every export format and from portable backups by default; a backup containing the voiceprofiles namespace is representable only with ADR-0071 password encryption, enforced in ExportService::create_portable_backup; the archive secret scanner refuses embedding-shaped blobs outside that namespace; restoring a voice-bearing archive re-runs the consent gate before profiles activate
rows.notes: Implemented (P2.3). `export_recording` carries resolved display-name text only; portable backups exclude the biometric tier by default and carry the name-only roster like any other library data (VP-077). The `voiceprofiles/` namespace is stageable only with a `VoiceProfilePermit`, which exists only for `Protection::Encrypted`, and `ArchiveBuilder::finish` refuses a plaintext emission that holds one — a plaintext backup containing voiceprints is unrepresentable rather than merely refused at the UI. `ArchiveSecretScanner` treats an embedding-shaped value outside that namespace as a fatal finding. Restoring voice data re-arms the consent gate before the rows land, so the feature is off until the user passes it in the target library. Residual, documented: an archive's ciphertext is only as unreadable as the key is unavailable — the key never travels, so a restore onto another machine yields rows that cannot decrypt.

rows.threat: Voice-profile poisoning: the wrong person enrolled into a profile, mislabelling them in every later recording
rows.control: Enrolment enforces minimum clean single-speaker speech and excludes overlap; matches are persisted suggestions that never change a transcript without explicit confirmation; every exemplar keeps provenance (recording, cluster, span) and a profile can be split by provenance; rejections are remembered and feed per-profile calibration; the UI never presents a match as identity
rows.notes: Planned by docs/specs/VOICE_PROFILES_SPEC.md (VP-060 to VP-066, VP-094) and ADR-0082. There is deliberately no auto-assignment tier at any score: measured demographic error disparity in VoxCeleb-trained models makes an auto-assignment threshold a policy about whose records get silently corrupted. The matching half of the control exists as of the P1.4 change in crates/app-core/src/voice_profiles/matching: suggestion-only bands, speech minima, model-version-mismatch refusal and bounded per-profile calibration, with golden and property tests in crates/app-core/tests/voice_matching.rs. The row stays planned because enrolment, exemplar provenance and remembered rejections still have no implementation and the owner file does not exist yet. The enrolment leg landed with P1.5: crates/app-core/src/voice_profiles/enroll.rs enforces the VP-065 minima from the stored reconciliation before the embedder is called, records provenance (recording, run, cluster, span) per exemplar and splits an enrolment by that provenance with the ciphertexts re-sealed under the new owner; the consent gate is a ConsentProof value with no public constructor, so the roster path cannot reach embedding code at all, and a scripted embedder that panics on call proves it at runtime in both closed states. A rejection is kept as a score record and feeds the per-profile offset the matcher reads. Remaining: the egui surfaces that present suggestions and the dedupe/merge disclosures (P2.1), and the real ONNX embedder.

rows.threat: Cross-library correlation of voiceprints: two libraries' profile stores combined to track one voice across contexts
rows.control: No sync and no stable cross-library identifier exist; each library has its own AEAD key; voice data is excluded from exports by default and representable only inside password-encrypted backups, so there is no plaintext artifact to correlate; the residual risk that a user restores one encrypted backup into two libraries is documented rather than denied
rows.notes: Export leg implemented (P2.3): plaintext voice export is unrepresentable, the per-library AEAD key never travels in an archive, and a restore re-runs the consent gate, so there is no plaintext artifact to correlate across libraries. Remaining: the no-stable-identifier posture is asserted by construction rather than by a test, and the documented residual risk stands — a user who restores one encrypted backup into two libraries has, by their own action, two copies of the same profiles (ADR-0080).
